headline: LA Gets New Free Veterinary Clinic From $2.5M Donation
meta_description: A $2.5 million gift has opened an ASPCA veterinary clinic in Los Angeles, offering free and low-cost pet care to people who cannot afford treatment.
summary_short: A major donation has opened a new ASPCA veterinary clinic in Los Angeles, providing free and low-cost care for pets whose owners struggle to pay for treatment.
body:
A $2.5 million donation has opened a new ASPCA veterinary clinic in Los Angeles, bringing free and low-cost veterinary care to pet owners who cannot otherwise afford treatment.

The clinic addresses a real gap in access to care. Many people who rely on limited resources struggle to provide basic medical attention for their animals, sometimes choosing between affording their pets' healthcare and meeting their own needs. The new facility in Los Angeles now removes that barrier for families in the community.

Beyond helping individual pet owners, the clinic also extends support to homeless populations, recognizing that people experiencing homelessness often have beloved pets they want to keep healthy. By providing care without the obstacle of cost, the ASPCA clinic strengthens bonds between people and their animals while ensuring these pets receive the medical attention they need.
quick_facts: $2.5 million donation funded the new clinic
Offers free and low-cost veterinary care
Serves pet owners unable to afford treatment
Also helps homeless people with their pets
